# E0315: wrong number of arguments

A call gives one argument per parameter, in order, since Stilt has no default arguments and no overloading.

- Rule: [`expressions.arguments`](../../reference/08-expressions.md#expressions.arguments)
- Reported at: the call, the closure or the variant pattern.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0315:3
fn area(width: i64, height: i64) -> i64 { width * height }

fn square(side: i64) -> i64 { area(side) }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn area(width: i64, height: i64) -> i64 { width * height }

fn square(side: i64) -> i64 { area(side, side) }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0315_print_with_several_arguments.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0315_print_with_several_arguments.lt):

```text
── WRONG NUMBER OF ARGUMENTS ── E0315_print_with_several_arguments.lt:3:3  [E0315]

`print` takes one string, which holds the values, as `print("a is {a}")`:

  3 │   print("a is", a)
    │   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A string inserts the value of each `{…}` in it, so one string says it all.

To fix it, write one string:

  3 │   print("a is {a}")
    │         ~~~~~~~~~~
```

`stilt check` on [`E0315_wrong_number_of_arguments.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0315_wrong_number_of_arguments.lt):

```text
── WRONG NUMBER OF ARGUMENTS ── E0315_wrong_number_of_arguments.lt:3:31  [E0315]

This takes 2 arguments, but 1 is given:

  3 │ fn square(side: i64) -> i64 { area(side) }
    │                               ^^^^^^^^^^

A call gives one argument per parameter, in order, since Stilt has no default
arguments and no overloading.
```
